full_judgment:
15. On appeal by the manufacturing companies the case went up to the House of Lords (F Hoffman La Roche vs Secretary of State for Trade and Industry 1974 2 All ER 1128. Lord Diplock observed; "My Lords, I think it leads to confusion to use such terms as 'voidable ad initio, 'void' or a 'nullity' as descriptive of the legal status of sub-ordinate legislation alleged to be ultra vires for patent or latent defects, before its validity has been pronounced on by a court of competent jurisdiction. These are concepts developed in the private law of contract which are ill-adapted to the field of public law. All that can usefully be said is that the presumption that sub-ordinate legislation is intra vires prevails in the absence of rebuttal, and that it cannot be rebutted by a party to legal proceedings in a court of competent jurisdiction who has locus standi to challenge the validity of the sub-ordinate legislation in question." 

 "A part from express provision in the governing statute, locus standi to challenge the validity of sub-ordinate legislation the validity of sub-ordinate legislation may be restricted, under the court's inherent power to control its own procedure, to a particular category of persons affected by the sub-ordinate legislation, and if none of these persons chooses to challenge it the presumption of validity prevails. Such was the case in Durayappah vs Fernando where on an appeal from Ceylon, although the Privy Council was of opinion that an order of the Minister was ultra vires owing to a latent defect in the procedure prior to its being made, they nevertheless treated it as having legal effect because the party who sought to challenge it had, in their view, no locus standi to do so." 

 "it is true enough that a piece of sub-ordinate legislation is presumed to be valid against persons who have no locus standi to challenge it; the puzzling case of Durayappah vs Fernando (1967) 2 All ER 152 can be understood as exemplifying this. But it is quite another matter to say. And I know of no supporting authority, that such a presumption exists when the validity of the sub-ordinate legislation is legitimately in question before a court and is challenged by a person who has locus standi to challenge it." 

 32. When a law is challenged as unconstitutional there is a presumption in favour of its constitutionality. There is also a presumption that the legislature knows best the needs, requirements and aspirations of the people on whose suffrage it comes into being. When the court examines the constitutionality of a legislation it does not claim that it is wiser than the legislature nor does it assume to exercise any right of veto on the power of the legislature. The Constitution has itself provided in Article 26 that all existing laws inconsistent with the provision of Part III shall to the extent of such inconsistency become void on its commencement, and the State shall not make any law inconsistent with any provision of Part III. (The combined effects of Articles 26, 44 and 102 of the Constitution is that the Court is required under the Constitution to enforce the fundamental rights conferred by Part III) 

 35. Mr Additional Attorney-General has referred to Ratnaprova Devi vs State of Orissa AIR 1964 (SC) 1195. In this case the Indian Supreme Court refused to declare the Orissa Private Land of Rulers (Assessment of Rent) Act 1958 as unconstitutional because of Article 14 of the Constitution of India when the petitioners failed to displace the initial presumption of constitutionality of an Act, and it was found fair and equitable tests were laid down for determining the rent in section 6 of the Act.
